verses.eng: – Sara, why are you laughing at my words? –
Scared, Sara replied:
– I did not laugh my lord!

—Don’t say you didn’t laugh, because I saw you laughing inside the store. – The
pilgrim affirmed.

Conscious of being in front of someone who knew his interior, Sara asked him:
 20 – Who are you Adanay?!

– I am the flame that broke away from the Fire of the Altar to be in your husband’s
vase! I am the Messiah / Anointed One, the Yahawah who suffers humiliation and contempt for love of
His people! –

Having made this revelation, the pilgrim extended His hands over Sharah’s head to
bless her; Only until then I saw that they were marked by scars similar to those of the
king of Shalam.

The pilgrim, with much tenderness, began to speak to the heart of my beloved,
rescuing her from her cave of disbelief:

– Sara, you are valuable in my eyes! All your past of disbelief and infertility is
forgiven! I have a glorious future for you, for you will become the mother of many
peoples and nations! –

After saying these words, the noble visitor went to the vase and, bowing, took from
him the three remaining pearls. Addressing Sara, he handed her two pearls, and said:
One is for you and the other is for your son Yatzachaq. –

Ahalay-Ab life transformed by Yahawah’s love, Sara prostrated herself at the feet of the
pilgrim who had saved her at the last moment of opportunity. When I saw her prostrate
submissive, my heart for so many years afflicted, it broke into tears of joy and gratitude,
and I fell at the feet of my Redeemer and King.

After comforting us with the certainty of our eternal salvation, the pilgrim handed me
the last pearl. When I squeezed it in my hands I felt a great light of joy and peace
penetrate my whole being, and I began to praise the Eternal for the certainty that I
would forever have my dear Sara and the son of the promise that, within One year would
be born.

After these things, Yahawah said goodbye to Sara and the shepherds who were there,
and invited me to accompany them to the hill facing the valley. When we arrived at that
place, the Eternal said goodbye to his two companions, sending them on a special
mission in Sadam.

From the top of the mountain we contemplated the fertile valleys and forests that, like
a paradise, stretched on both banks of the Yaradan River, surrounding the thriving cities,
within which Sadam and Imarah stood out.
 3 It was on that hill that, after the fight between my shepherds and the shepherds of Lawat,
I gave him the opportunity to choose the course to follow, because we could not stay
together. Attracted by the riches of the countryside, he decided to move there.

Looking at my companion who remained silent from the moment we saw the
countryside, I was surprised to see him crying. I asked him the reason for his sadness,
and He, sobbing replied:

– This is for me a very sad day, for for the last time my eyes can rest on this fertile
valley. I cry for the inhabitants of those cities who don’t know their days will end! –

Yahawah’s statement brought back the memory of all those captives who had been
released six years before; unfortunately, almost everyone rejected the purification bath,
returning filthy to their homes; Only Lawat and his daughters accepted salvation, taking
possession of their pearls. Thinking about some possibility of liberation for that people, I
asked the Adanay:
– And if there are in those cities, fifty just people, would they still be destroyed? –
Yahawah told me that if there were fifty righteous, the entire plain would be forgiven.
– What if there are 45 fair? –
—If there were 45 righteous, all those cities would be forgiven. –

I continued with my inquiries until I reached number ten. Yahawah told me that if
there were 10 righteous in those cities, the entire plain would be forgiven.

Tortured by an inexpressible agony of spirit, Yahawah again wept bitterly, while in a
seized voice he uttered a sad regret:

—Sodoma and Imarah, how many times I wanted to gather your children, like the
chicken that gathers its chicks under its wings, but you did not accept my protection.
Dan is it that you changed the light of my salvation, for the darkness of this kingdom of
death?! My ears are attentive in search of at least one prayer, but everything is silence!
My hands are extended, ready to prevent the fire of judgment, but you reject my help! –

Leaning next to my suffering companion, I joined Him in lamentation. In that moment
of pain, I was certain that Malakay-Tzadaq also suffered for all those who had changed the
love and peace of Shalam, for the illusions of that valley of destruction.

After a long cry, Yahawah comforted me, with the revelation of his two companions,
they were at that time in Sadam, with the mission of saving Lawat and his daughters
freeing them from death. His words brought me great relief, and I fell grateful to his feet.

—Take an empty scroll and record in it the history of the vase and the history of Shalam,
as you heard from Malakay-Tzadaq’s lips. Within a year, you and all those who will accept
salvation must go up to Shalam for Sukot’s feast; On that day, they will return the vase to
the king of Shalam, offering the scroll inside him as a present. –

That same afternoon, in obedience to Yahawah’s orders, I began to record the story
lived by me and my shepherds, from the moment I left for the valley, carrying the vase
with its flare on its back.

The next day, the sun was already high, when, mentioning the city of Sadam in the
manuscript, I remembered that this was the day of its destruction. Ahalay-Ab my heart racing,
I ran over there and was frightened by the scenario that stretched before my eyes:
Instead of that fertile valley, similar to a paradise, there was an smoking desert, lifeless;
Instead of the cities of Sadam and Imarah, there was a deep crater, where the salty
sea waters dripped.

Broken at that vision of destruction, I returned to the store with a sad heart. The
memory of so many people who, by rejecting divine forgiveness, had been consumed by
fire, left me deeply weakened. In the following days, I found no strength to write; I
returned to the hill other times, hoping that all this was a nightmare, but instead of the
fertile valley I could only perceive that chaos.

It took several days for me to return to the spirit of continuing with the writings of the
scroll.

This is the story of Shalam as I heard it from Malakay-Tzadaq’s lips on the occasion of
Sukot’s party, fifteen days after the release of Lawat and his daughters.

It all started with a dream in the heart of an man named Adanayah; He possessed many
riches, but he appreciated nothing more than the justice and peace that were born of
wisdom and love.

Tired of the injustices that prevailed throughout the land of Kanain, Adanayah decided
to build a kingdom that was governed by laws of love and justice. The name of the
capital of that kingdom would be Shalam, the City of Peace.

Shalam’s subjects would not wield bows and arrows, but would be trained in musical art;
Each inhabitant of Shalam would always have at his fingertips a musical instrument, to
express through him the peace and joy of that new kingdom. Together, they would form
a powerful orchestra in the fight against disharmony born of pride and selfishness.

The first step of Adonias for the concretization of his plan, was to elaborate the laws of
the new kingdom, which he wrote them in a parchment. Shalam’s subjects could not lie,
steal, hate, or kill their fellowmen. Pride and selfishness were indicated as the cause of
all evil, therefore, they could not exist in that place of peace.

The laws of parchment required the practice of humility, sincerity, friendship, and,
above all, the love that is the greatest of all virtues.
 7 After registering on the parchment the laws that would govern that kingdom, Adonias
began to plan the architecture of Shalam. It would be a city at first small, with rooms for
one thousand two hundred people. As the place of its construction, an high region of
Kanain, west of the Mount of Olives, was chosen.

In a short time, the realization of Adonias began to attract people from all over the
world who, from near and far, came to know the palaces and mansions that were being
built. Admired by the beauty of that white city, visitors asked about who their inhabitants
would be. Adanayah showed them the scroll, saying that Shalam was destined for the clean
of heart — those who were willing to obey his laws. –

The building of the city was finally completed and Shalam proved beautiful as an ornate
bride, waiting for her husband.
